data_provenance: Δ-scores from live Liganx baseline. Osimertinib is COVALENT on C797. Rigid-receptor Δ understates the resistance signal for C797S (acrylamide warhead loses its target) — documented method limit. ESM2 + literature prior carry more weight here.

predicted_resistance.rationale: THE on-target Osimertinib resistance event. Cysteine→Serine substitution ablates the covalent acrylamide bond. Single-nt-accessible (TGC→AGC). Vina's Δ at +0.2 is below the noise floor — the cellular IC50 shift is >100× (Thress 2015, Nat Med). This is the case where the literature prior dominates the calibrated forecast.

Solvent-front residue; emerging Osimertinib resistance pathway (Wang 2017). Two-nucleotide path means lower mutational accessibility than single-nt events — would emerge later and at lower frequency than C797S, which matches observed clinical timeline.
Single-nucleotide-accessible alternative at the L792 hotspot. Mutant-receptor build failed in baseline (pending pipeline fix). Expected mechanism mirror of L792H.

covalent_caveat: Osimertinib's WT-vs-T790M selectivity is engineered around T790M's methionine bulk + a covalent acrylamide bond to C797. Vina sees only the geometric component. The atlas's calibrated layer (Δ + ESM2 fitness + accessibility + literature prior) is designed precisely for this kind of multi-mechanism resistance.
ledger_note: Osimertinib has the cleanest resistance-prediction story in oncology: C797S was structurally predictable on day one of approval, appeared clinically within 18 months, and remains the dominant on-target resistance event. The atlas captures this and uses it as a calibration anchor for forecasting resistance to next-generation covalent inhibitors.
